module_title: Medicines and Drugs in Everyday Life
introduction: When we fall sick, the chemicals we consume to interact with our biological targets are called medicines. Competitive exams ask direct questions about the medical categories of common drugs.

core_concepts.title: Antipyretics
core_concepts.description:
These are drugs that lower body temperature during a 'Fever'. 
Examples: Paracetamol, Aspirin.

core_concepts.title: Analgesics
core_concepts.description:
These are drugs that relieve 'Pain' without causing the loss of consciousness. 
Examples: Ibuprofen, Aspirin, Diclofenac. (Note: Aspirin works as both an analgesic and an antipyretic).

core_concepts.title: Antibiotics
core_concepts.description:
These are chemical substances produced by microbes that kill or inhibit the growth of other 'Bacteria'. They do NOT work against viruses. 
Example: Penicillin (The first antibiotic, discovered by Alexander Fleming).

core_concepts.title: Antiseptics vs. Disinfectants
core_concepts.description:
1. Antiseptics: Applied to 'living tissues' (wounds, cuts, skin) to kill or prevent the growth of microbes. (e.g., Dettol, Tincture of Iodine). 
2. Disinfectants: Applied to 'non-living objects' (floors, drainage systems, toilets). (e.g., 1% solution of Phenol).

important_entities.name: Antacids
important_entities.significance: To neutralize the burning sensation caused by excess $HCl$ in the stomach, we take mild alkaline drugs called Antacids (like Eno or Digene). The most prominent active ingredient is 'Milk of Magnesia' ($Mg(OH)_2$).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Aspirin is an analgesic and antipyretic, but it has another extremely important property—it is an 'Anti-blood clotting agent' (blood thinner). That is why it is widely used to prevent 'Heart Attacks'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A 'pyre' is a fire. So, an Anti-pyretic is something that fights the fire (fever/heat) inside your body.

exam_strategy_tips: Repeatedly asked in State PCS and Railways: 'Dettol is a mixture of which two chemicals?' Answer: Chloroxylenol and Terpineol.
